The paper was published in Materials and Design, Volume 24, 2003, pages 391-396
The research was conducted by authors from Tsinghua University, Harbin Institute of Technology, and Harbin Engineering University in China
The basic absorbing structure studied is a single-layer homogeneous absorber (SLHA) backed by a perfect conducting plate
The first design principle requires coating thickness d = λ/4 ÷ sin(2β) for quasi-standing wave formation
Matching conditions require tan(δₑ) = tan(δₘ) = tan(δᵢ) for ideal absorption
The reflection index R is expressed in decibels as R_dB = 20 lg|R|
Electric field amplitude is zero at the coating-conducting plate interface and maximum at the free space interface
Magnetic field amplitude at the free space interface is E₀/Z₀
Phase difference between electric and magnetic fields can reach approximately 90° at the conducting plate interface
The propagation constant in the coating is decomposed as γ = α + iβ, where α is attenuation and β is phase factor
Wave impedance Z varies continuously with position within the coating and matches free space impedance Z₀ at the surface
Dispersion parameters k₁ and k₂ characterize deviations from ideal matching conditions
When k₁ = k₂ = 1, ideal matching is achieved with zero reflection
Larger tan(δₘ) values are more beneficial for controlling absorption performance when tan(δₑ) ≠ tan(δₘ)
The slope of absorption curves changes rapidly when tan(δₑ) > tan(δₘ) and slowly when tan(δₑ) < tan(δₘ)
Practical coatings typically satisfy matching conditions only at specific frequency points, not across broad bands
The character impedance of free space is Z₀ = (μ₀/ε₀)^(1/2)
The character impedance of the coating is Z = (μ/ε)^(1/2)
Attenuation factor α = (π/2d)·tan(δ) under matching conditions
Phase factor β = ν·√(ε'μ') = π/(2d) under matching conditions
The paper provides equations for electromagnetic parameters as functions of desired attenuation level A (in dB)
Constants C and D in the design equations are derived from impedance matching conditions
The quasi-standing wave condition is essential for achieving orthogonality of electric and magnetic field components
Mismatching analysis shows that absorption performance decreases with increasing parameter dispersion
The design rules have applications in both material research and practical coating design
